channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.title: Google patches eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in attacks this year
item.description: Google has released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks, the eighth such flaw since the start of the year.

item.title: CISA Flags SonicWall SonicOS MFA Bypass Flaw Amid Reports of Possible Exploitation
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a high-severity vulnerability impacting SonicWall SonicOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, following reports that it said may have been exploited in real-world attacks. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-19868 (CVSS…

item.title: IBM Aspera Faspex, SignalWire FreeSwitch Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks
item.description: CISA has added CVE-2026-123218 and CVE-2026-116779 to KEV, urging federal agencies to patch them within three days. The post IBM Aspera Faspex, SignalWire FreeSwitch Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Hackers exploit SSHole OpenSSH flaw to breach Linux systems
item.description: Hackers are actively exploiting the "SSHole" vulnerability (CVE-2026-123158) in OpenSSH to execute commands, steal credentials, and establish persistent access.

item.title: Exploited Outlook Zero-Day Among 1,094 Flaws Patched by Microsoft
item.description: CVE-2026-124194 is the Outlook zero-day for which Microsoft says it’s aware of active exploitation. The post Exploited Outlook Zero-Day Among 1,094 Flaws Patched by Microsoft appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day
item.description: Today is Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, with security updates addressing a record-breaking 1,235 flaws, including one actively exploited Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability.

item.title: Critical Xen Orchestra auth bypass flaw exploited to hijack VM servers
item.description: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks that could grant administrator privileges and allow takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts.

item.title: Attackers Exploit AhsayCBS Flaws to Deploy Sandbox-Evading Python Backdoor
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of an attack that exploited two now-patched vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS to deliver a Python-based implant. The activity, observed by Huntress in October 2026, involves the exploitation of a chain comprising CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 to bypass authentication…

item.title: CVE-2026-105588 Windows DHCP Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description: Missing authentication for critical function in Windows DHCP Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Patched Apple Flaw to Deliver Info-Stealing Malware, CISA Says
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Wednesday added a medium-severity security flaw impacting multiple Apple operating systems to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, following reports of active exploitation. The vulnerability in question is CVE-2024-27834 (CVSS score…

item.title: CVE-2026-109463 Windows DNS Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: Deserialization of untrusted data in Windows DNS allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

item.title: N-able Takes N-central Offline as Researcher Drops Over 30 Zero-Days
item.description: Attackers could exploit the flaws for remote code execution, credential theft, and administrator account creation. The post N-able Takes N-central Offline as Researcher Drops Over 30 Zero-Days appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Fireworks AI discloses new breach after cloud provider hack
item.description: AI infrastructure startup Fireworks has disclosed a new security breach in which attackers accessed its development machines after breaching a third-party cloud provider.

item.title: AI company Fireworks says hackers stole data, billing info during October breaches
item.description: Fireworks said the incident affected a “limited number of customer accounts” — all of whom were notified of the attack.

item.title: CVE-2026-100204 HEIF Image Extensions Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: Use after free in HEIF Image Extensions allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

item.title: CVE-2026-102868 Windows Shell Information Disclosure Vulnerability
item.description: Exposure of sensitive system information to an unauthorized control sphere in Windows Shell allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.

item.title: CVE-2026-105544 .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description: Improper access control in.NET allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

item.title: CVE-2026-105582 Windows DWM Core Library Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description: Release of invalid pointer or reference in Windows DWM Core Library allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

item.title: CVE-2026-105586 Microsoft Windows SCSI Class System File Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description: Null pointer dereference in Microsoft Windows SCSI Class System File allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

item.title: CVE-2026-105590 Windows Active Directory Certificate Services Security Feature Bypass
item.description: Improper certificate validation in Windows Active Directory Certificate Services allows an authorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

item.title: CVE-2026-108411 Microsoft ODBC Driver Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows ODBC Driver allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

item.title: CVE-2026-109467 Azure DevOps Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: Improper authentication in Azure DevOps allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

item.title: CVE-2026-114166 Microsoft Raw Image Extension Information Disclosure Vulnerability
item.description: Buffer over-read in Windows Raw Image Extension allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information locally.

item.title: CVE-2026-84004 AMD Zen Information Disclosure Vulnerability
item.description: Processor optimization removal or modification of security-critical code in AMD Zen allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.

item.title: Fireworks AI Breach Widens to Expose Customer Billing Data and Incomplete Model Weights
item.description: Fireworks AI disclosed on Monday that its investigation into a security incident first reported early last month uncovered further malicious activity, affecting account and billing information, alongside secrets, datasets, and incomplete models for a "limited set of accounts." item.title: SAP Patches Critical ICM2SHELL, ProxyGate Vulnerabilities
item.description: SAP has published 42 new and updated security advisories, including nine that address critical-severity vulnerabilities. The post SAP Patches Critical ICM2SHELL, ProxyGate Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.description: The Russia-aligned state-sponsored threat actor known as Turla (aka Snake) is wielding a previously undocumented cyber espionage toolset called Cereal that's used to break into victims' Microsoft Exchange servers with an aim to surreptitiously collect emails. item.title: N-able takes cloud platform offline after 30+ "zero-days" published
item.description: N-able has taken its hosted N-central environments offline and urged on-premises customers to shut down their servers after a security researcher publicly disclosed more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities, including exploits that could let attackers take over vulnerable systems.

item.description: Microsoft’s FORGE Lab found several memory safety issues in Rust’s standard library (std and core), including cases where code written entirely in safe Rust can trigger undefined behavior. The research used Hyenas, FORGE’s frontier research version of codename MDASH, an AI-powered vulnerability-scanning system. The…

item.title: Binance denies data breach after alleged ShinyHunters claims
item.description: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, has denied claims of a new security breach made by a threat actor using the 'ShinyHunters' handle on a newly emerged underground cybercrime forum.

item.title: Hackers Exploiting ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass in OpenSSH
item.description: The initial exploitation attempts are attributed to botnets and crypto miners, but other threat actors are expected to follow suit. The post Hackers Exploiting ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass in OpenSSH appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates released
item.description: Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 and cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs, and add new features.

item.title: Ransomware recovery is now a client retention metric
item.description: Recovering from ransomware doesn't guarantee an MSP will retain its clients, especially when delays, poor communication, and unexpected costs undermine trust. Kaseya examines how disconnected recovery tools create these problems and how integrated workflows can improve response times, transparency, and client…

item.title: Russian hackers compromised government email servers to steal NATO, EU correspondence
item.description: Russian state-linked hackers have compromised government email servers in Romania and Kazakhstan to secretly intercept messages exchanged with NATO and European Union officials, researchers said.

item.title: Hackers now exploit critical Barracuda ESG flaws to gain root access
item.description: Cybersecurity company Barracuda Networks warned that attackers have begun exploiting two recently patched Email Security Gateway (ESG) vulnerabilities that let them run commands with root privileges.

item.title: Vanderbilt University hit in BYOD ransomware attack, data theft claimed
item.description: Vanderbilt University warns it is responding to a cyberattack claimed by the BYOD ransomware gang, which claims to have encrypted the university's databases and stolen sensitive student, employee, and research data.
